title: Add contextualization workflows, embedded playground snippets, and structured-output linter
author: Maya Thompson
description: This PR adds a new developer-facing documentation section that demonstrates pragmatic contextualization workflows and small reproducible playground snippets for RAG-style agents. Motivation: teams building retrieval-augmented features often struggle to reason about context window usage, metadata selection, and how to validate tool-calls / structured output. This change bundles: 1) 'Contextualization Workflows' guide with prescriptive recipes for short/medium/long contexts and eviction strategies; 2) an embedded interactive playground pattern (static examples + live iframe hooks) that can be dropped into docs pages or the examples repo to allow quick local prototyping; 3) a lightweight structured-output linter (docs rule + config examples) that validates model tool-call JSON shapes, required fields, and a configurable tolerance for extra keys to reduce brittle downstream parsing. Checklist: - [x] Add contextualization guide with examples and diagrams - [x] Add 6 compact playground snippets (TS + Python) demonstrating deterministic replay and prefix caching - [x] Implement docs-side linter rules and include example .structlinter.yaml - [x] Add CI smoke test that runs one example in headless mode and validates output against schema - [x] Update docs navigation and TOC entry - [x] Add release notes entry and a short how-to for customer-facing solutions engineering. Related: references ENG-11842 (workload patterns), DOC-3321 (docs refresh).
commits: 6 commits: 1) scaffold contextualization guide and assets; 2) add playground JS/TS/Python snippets and a minimal in-browser shim; 3) add .structlinter schema and rule runner for docs CI; 4) wire playground iframe examples into docs pages; 5) add smoke test harness and CI job; 6) docs polish and copy edits.

release_notes: Add contextualization guide and embedded playgrounds for faster RAG prototyping; introduce structured-output linter for docs examples (configurable to allow extra keys).
